pages.quiz:
INTEGRATED SCIENCE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT 3
====

EXAM BODY: KJSEA
GRADE: Grade 8 JSS
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30

INSTRUCTIONS
----
• Answer all questions.
• For calculations, show full working (formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units).
• Diagrams provided are part of the question — use every labeled value.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. A chemical reaction that forms a precipitate
   D. Heating a solid until it melts

2. In osmosis, what mainly moves across a selectively permeable membrane? (1 mark)
   A. Water
   B. Sand grains
   C. Whole sugar crystals only
   D. Electric current

3. Eyepiece ×5 and objective ×40. What is total magnification? (1 mark)
   A. ×200
   B. ×45
   C. ×5
   D. ×80

4. Calculate pressure when F = 140 N and A = 0.4 m². (1 mark)
   A. 350 Pa
   B. 56 Pa
   C. 140.4 Pa
   D. 0.002857142857142857 Pa

[DIAGRAM]

PURPOSE: Show force F = 140 N acting on area A = 0.4 m² with P = F/A labeled.
ALT: Force arrow of 140 newtons pressing on a rectangular area of 0.4 square metres.

5. The main energy chain in a simple torch is: (1 mark)
   A. Chemical → electrical → light (+ heat)
   B. Light → chemical → sound
   C. Sound → nuclear → light
   D. Heat → food → electricity only

6. Iron has symbol Fe from the Latin name: (1 mark)
   A. Ferrum
   B. Natrium
   C. Aurum
   D. Kalium

7. Which statement correctly defines an element? (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical or physical means
   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. A substance that always conducts electricity

8. A learner writes calcium as CA. What is the correct symbol and rule? (1 mark)
   A. Ca — first letter capital, second letter small
   B. CA — both letters must be capitals
   C. ca — both letters must be small
   D. C — calcium uses only one letter

9. Why is table salt (NaCl) classified as a compound? (1 mark)
   A. It contains sodium and chlorine chemically joined in a fixed ratio
   B. It is white and looks pure
   C. It melts when heated
   D. It is mined at Lake Magadi only

10. Which change is physical? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Iron rusting
   D. Baking soda reacting with vinegar to make a new gas

SECTION B — STRUCTURED QUESTIONS
----
11. Define osmosis and describe what happens to visking tubing with concentrated sugar solution in distilled water. (6 marks)

12. Trace the energy transformations in a torch from dry cells to the bulb. (5 marks)

13. Differentiate an element from a compound. Give one Kenyan example of each. (5 marks)

14. Explain why melting ice is a physical change but burning paper is a chemical change. (6 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. Correct option: A — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

2. Correct option: A — Water

3. Correct option: A — ×200
Working:
1. Formula / relationship: Total magnification = eyepiece × objective
2. Substitute values: Total = 5 × 40
3. Total = 200
Final Answer: ×200
Marks: M1 multiply; A1 answer

4. Correct option: A — 350 Pa
Working:
1. Formula / relationship: P = F / A
2. Substitute values: P = 140 / 0.4
3. P = 350
Final Answer: 350 Pa
Marks: M1 substitute; A1 Pa

5. Correct option: A — Chemical → electrical → light (+ heat)

6. Correct option: A — Ferrum

7. Correct option: A — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical or physical means

8. Correct option: A — Ca — first letter capital, second letter small

9. Correct option: A — It contains sodium and chlorine chemically joined in a fixed ratio

10. Correct option: A — Ice melting to water

11. (6 marks)
Osmosis: water moves across a selectively permeable membrane from dilute toward more concentrated solution. Water enters the tubing; it swells/gains mass.

12. (5 marks)
Chemical energy (cells) → electrical energy (circuit) → light energy + heat energy (bulb).

13. (5 marks)
An element is a pure substance of one kind of atom and cannot be broken down chemically/physically into simpler substances (e.g. copper in wires, Fe in a jembe). A compound is made when different elements join chemically in fixed proportions (e.g. NaCl table salt, H₂O).

14. (6 marks)
Melting ice: still H₂O, no new substance, reversible by freezing → physical. Burning paper: ash/gases form, new substances, not simply reversible → chemical.
